articles.title: Murder in Okinawa: The US military’s history of alleged crime in Japan
articles.summary: The murder of 39-year-old Anna Yagi is the latest in a string of crimes involving US personnel on Okinawa.
articles.body:
The murder of a Japanese woman allegedly committed by a US Marine on the southern island of Okinawa has prompted public outrage in Japan, amid a long string of incidents involving American personnel.

Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi described the incident on Monday as a “heinous crime” and said the government had lodged a strong protest with Washington, urging their “full cooperation with the investigation” and “strict discipline among US military personnel”.

About 100 people participated in a rally in Naha, the capital of Okinawa, on Sunday, as news spread that a US marine had, a day earlier, allegedly killed a 39-year-old woman at a hotel in the city and stolen her wallet.

Public broadcaster NHK reported that security camera footage from near the scene showed a foreign man entering a room with a woman and later leaving alone with her belongings. Police then found a 20-year-old man who matched the description. The suspect has reportedly denied the allegations.

Police identified the suspect as Devin Jacob Ballard and the victim as Anna Yagi.

Kozue Akibayashi, a professor of gender and peace studies at Doshisha University in Kyoto, Japan, said the incident reflects a decades-long issue. “The Japanese government has always chosen the US-Japan alliance over the safety and lives, and voices of the people of Okinawa,” she told Al Jazeera.

Why are US marines stationed in Okinawa?

The United States has about 54,000 military personnel stationed in Japan. Okinawa bears a disproportionate burden, hosting about 70 percent of US military facilities in the country, set up under a bilateral security treaty and Status of Forces Agreement (SOFA) signed first in 1951 and then revised in 1960.

Japan has the “primary right to exercise jurisdiction” for crimes committed off-base while US personnel are not on duty, while the US has the “primary right” for crimes committed on the base or while on duty.

Okinawa is viewed by Tokyo and Washington as key in deterring potential military aggression from China. “The US and the Japanese governments have always cited ‘geopolitical’ importance of the location of the archipelago to justify not only the presence itself but also the disproportionately high concentration of the US military there,” Akibayashi, at Doshisha University, said.

“However, in reality, it was convenient for the Japanese government to keep the larger number of US troops and military facilities in Okinawa that nobody wants.”

The professor said Okinawa, one of Japan’s 47 prefectures, represents 1 percent of the entire population of Japan and less than 1 percent of the entire Japanese territory.

“Their political voice does not seem to bear significance to the Japanese government,” she added. “Probably more importantly, Okinawa was colonised by Japan in the late 19th century and has always been a subject of discrimination within Japan.”

Okinawa was historically an independent trading nation called the Ryukyu Kingdom before Japan annexed it in 1879. The US held Okinawa, which is ‌100 kilometres (60 miles) from Taiwan at the closest point, from the end of World War II ⁠until 1972.

“Many US military bases located on the main islands of Japan were transferred to the islands of Okinawa … because the mainland Japanese people had started to protest the presence of the US military in their neighbourhood,” Akibayashi said.

The presence of US marines has repeatedly stirred resentment among residents ⁠over issues such as noise, aircraft crashes and the conduct of personnel.

Have US marines been accused of crimes before?

Yes, there is a long history of crimes including rapes, assaults, hit-and-run and drunk-driving accidents allegedly committed by US personnel, triggering protests on Okinawa.

Last year, a Japanese court sentenced a US marine accused of choking and attempting to rape a woman in her 20s to seven years in prison.

In 2017, a former US marine and civilian military base worker was sentenced to life in prison for the rape and murder of a local woman in Okinawa. The same year, an intoxicated US marine crashed his vehicle into a mini-truck, killing its 61-year-old local driver.

In 1995, the rape of a 12-year-old Okinawan girl by three US servicemen led to mass protests.

According to the Yomiuri Shimbun newspaper, about 6,000 US military personnel have been arrested since 1972, when the US returned control of Okinawa to Japan. In 2024, the number of arrests hit 80, the highest in 20 years.

Akibayashi said people in Okinawa have been outraged by these crimes, which they see as violations of their basic human rights. “Their lives and even survival have been made insecure and threatened by the US military presence,” she said.

“They have expressed countless times their opposition to and anger at the US military presence, and unequal burden of ‘security’ policies imposed on them throughout the decades. Their protests have been ignored and nullified.”

How did Japan and the US respond to Yagi’s murder?

Japanese authorities have expressed outrage at the murder, while the US pledged full collaboration in the investigations.

Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said, “Incidents and accidents involving US military personnel cause great anxiety among the local community and must not be allowed to happen.”

Prime Minister Takaichi said Japan had lodged a protest with US authorities and called the crime “exceptionally brutal and vicious”.

The government has urged the US “to provide maximum cooperation with the investigation, enforce stricter discipline among US military personnel, and take thorough measures to prevent the recurrence of similar crimes”, Takaichi said.

The US embassy and the Marine Corps expressed condolences over the incident and said they were cooperating with the Japanese authorities.

The Marine Corps said in a statement that the suspect, who ⁠is assigned to the III Marine Expeditionary Force and based ⁠at Marine Corps Air Station Futenma, was in Japanese custody.

“The Marine Corps takes these allegations very seriously and expects every Marine to adhere to the highest standards of behavior,” it said.

US Ambassador George Glass posted on social media that he had spoken with Japan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Okinawa’s governor, offering “our sincere condolences and pledging full cooperation as the investigation continues”.

Akibayashi said that when crimes are committed, “the US government and the military always say they would address the issue or promise tighter discipline”.

articles.title: In 1971, West Virginia rebuilt Route 2 with power-plant bottom ash and boiler slag; the unconventional road base gave excellent service for more than 20 years at lower cost
articles.summary: Explore how West Virginia revolutionized road construction in 1971 by using bottom ash and boiler slag from power plants for Route 2, achieving durability and lower costs. Learn about this groundbreaking project and its lasting impact on highway infrastructure.
articles.body: A section of West Virginia Route 2 was rebuilt in 1971-72 using a mixture of bottom ash and boiler slag from power plants as aggregate for a Portland cement-stabilized base. The road later provided excellent service for more than 10 years, and by using ash-based material, construction costs were substantially reduced when compared to conventional aggregates. Representing a large-scale deployment of coal combustion byproducts in highway infrastructure, the project utilized aggregates supplied by American Electric Power Company’s Mitchell and Kammer plants.Bottom ash from one station was combined with boiler slag from the other and blended in order to meet the gradation requirements established by the West Virginia Department of Highways for cement-treated base courses. The FHWA record identifies the Route 2 project as a granular base project near Wheeling, West Virginia and the documented mixture contained about 54% boiler slag, 46% bottom ash, and 5% Portland cement by aggregate weight.Processing the ash for pavement use The FHWA 1997 guidelines described several requirements for the preparation of bottom ash and boiler slag for stabilized pavement applications. Both materials can be dewatered relatively quickly in one or two days, but ponded ash requires longer drainage because it can contain fly ash. In addition, for the finished mixture to be compacted properly, the material must also have a suitable particle-size distribution. Generally, bottom ash is more well graded in comparison to boiler slag, but it can also contain agglomerated or popcorn-like particles, which should be reduced in size or removed by screening as per the FHWA.On the other hand, boiler slag tends to have a uniform particle size between the No. 4 and No. 40 sieve sizes but if necessary the materials can be blended with other aggregates to obtain the specified gradation. Other materials to be removed before construction, identified by the agency was coal pyrites, which can oxidise or weather over time, leading to expansion and possible popouts from the pavement matrix. While some bottom ash also contains soluble sulfates, which when present in detrimental qualities can be concerning.The engineering properties of materials were also documented: bottom ash generally had a specific gravity between 2.1 and 2.7, while boiler slag generally ranged from 2.3 to 2.9. In abrasion testing, bottom ash recorded losses between 30% and 50%, and boiler slag between 24% and 48%. Since bottom ashes had losses below 45%, they met the ASTM requirements for soil-aggregate base and subbase materials.West Virginia expanded the use of cement-stabilized ash The Route 2 project was followed by the additional use of cement-stabilized bottom ash in West Virginia. Beginning in 1984, several hundred miles of low-volume secondary roads were reconstructed using cement-stabilized bottom ash, and most carried between 150 and 1,500 vehicles per day. The FHWA cited Route 34 in Putnam County near Charleston as an example where a 150-millimeter bottom ash subbase was placed and compacted, followed by successive 150-millimeter lifts of cement-treated bottom ash on top of it.Moreover, West Virginia was not the only state to use bottom ash and boiler slag in pavement; a 1992 survey found that other states, including Arkansas, Kentucky, Mississippi, Texas and Utah used bottom ash as a stabilized base or subbase application. In addition, reports also found that in 1996 approximately 0.6 million metric tons of bottom ash and boiler slag were being used as a road base or subbase, although the exact share used in stabilized applications was not identified. Ultimately, the Route 2 reconstruction demonstrated the use of bottom ash and boiler slag in a cement-stabilized base.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Five adopted Black children abused by white parents awarded $4.4 million settlement after CPS failures in West Virginia; some were forced to live in a shed without running water or a bathroom
articles.summary: Five children who were subjected to years of abuse and neglect by their adoptive parents in West Virginia have been awarded a $4.4 million settlement from
articles.body: Five children who were subjected to years of abuse and neglect by their adoptive parents in West Virginia have been awarded a $4.4 million settlement from the state Department of Human Services following failures by Child Protective Services to adequately respond to reports about their welfare.Kanawha County Circuit Judge Maryclaire Akers approved the settlement on Tuesday. The amount, which will be divided among the five children, represents the maximum compensation available to each child through the state’s Board of Risk Management, according to West Virginia Watch.The case involved a white couple, Jeanne Kay Whitefeather, 63, and Donald Lantz, 64, who were accused of keeping their adopted Black children in deplorable conditions and treating them in what prosecutors described as slave-like circumstances. Some of the children were forced to live in a shed without running water or a bathroom.Neighbours repeatedly raised concernsNeighbours had reportedly contacted CPS multiple times over concerns about the children, but said they did not receive meaningful follow-up. The children were ultimately discovered by law enforcement in October 2023.Whitefeather and Lantz were later convicted and received the maximum sentences, amounting to decades in prison, for their treatment of the children.Attorney Dante’ diTrapano, who represented the victims, said the settlement could give the children an opportunity to recover from the trauma they experienced.“It means that these kids will have an opportunity to be children,” diTrapano said. “They were robbed of their innocence and robbed of their youth by the monsters that were their former parents.”The settlement is expected to help pay for the children’s ongoing needs as they rebuild their lives. According to diTrapano, several of the children require significant support because of trauma associated with the abuse.Lawsuit highlighted alleged CPS failuresDiTrapano filed the lawsuit against the West Virginia Department of Human Services, arguing that CPS failed to properly respond to multiple warnings about the children.West Virginia Watch previously reported that DoHS was unable to produce documentation showing CPS had made contact with the children after receiving a referral concerning alleged slave-like conditions at the home.Evidence presented during the adoptive parents’ criminal trial reportedly showed that CPS left a card at the family's door. DiTrapano said there were numerous calls from neighbours but only limited follow-up.“There were a ton of calls that came in from neighbors, and I think only one visit out there. There should have been many more,” he said.He also alleged that CPS later interviewed the children within earshot of their adoptive parents, raising further concerns about how the investigation was conducted.State says child welfare system has undergone changesLars Dalseide, spokesperson for West Virginia Gov. Patrick Morrisey, said the Department of Human Services does not comment on specific legal settlements or ongoing litigation.The case predates the Morrisey administration. Dalseide said the employee involved in the case was terminated by the previous administration.He also pointed to changes made under the current administration, including restructuring leadership, establishing clearer expectations across regions and strengthening training for frontline workers.The administration has also begun using the “SAFE Model” to assess child welfare cases, with the stated goal of creating a more consistent approach to decision-making.“The safety and well-being of West Virginia’s children remain our highest priorities,” Dalseide said. “DoHS will continue evaluating its policies, oversight and operations and making changes where needed to better protect children and support families.”DiTrapano, however, argued that broader changes are still necessary.“The whole system is broken,” he said, calling for improvements in the quality of child welfare personnel, interviewing procedures and documentation practices.“They have to take these calls seriously,” he added.Children now living with new adoptive familiesThe five children have since been placed with new adoptive families, according to diTrapano. Two of their new adoptive mothers spoke in court about the children's lives following their removal from the abusive household, including a trip to the beach.“It means everything to us to be able to help these kids,” diTrapano said.The attorney and the Salango Law Firm also plan to pursue legal action against Washington state's Human Services Department. DiTrapano alleges that the agency approved the couple's transfer of children from Washington to West Virginia despite previous reports of child abuse involving them.Unlike West Virginia, Washington does not have a monetary damage cap in such cases, potentially allowing the children to seek additional compensation if the lawsuit succeeds.Lawmaker plans to reintroduce Child Captivity Prevention ActThe case has also prompted renewed calls for legislative changes in West Virginia.Del. Hollis Lewis, D-Kanawha, said he plans to reintroduce the Child Captivity Prevention Act in 2027. The proposed legislation would require families moving to West Virginia who intend to homeschool their children to notify the Department of Human Services.Whitefeather and Lantz had homeschooled the children before police discovered the abuse.Lewis previously introduced the legislation during the state's 2026 legislative session, but it did not advance before lawmakers adjourned in March.“We’re for parents having options about how they wish to educate their children, but we are also for sensible, common sense guidelines and provisions to ensure that you know those educational choices don’t lead to abuse,” Lewis said.Lewis also credited residents in Sissonville who repeatedly alerted authorities to the conditions at the couple's home.“The community was the one that actually blew the whistle on this,” he said, adding that without those efforts, the children could potentially have remained in the abusive situation.The $4.4 million settlement now provides the five victims with financial resources to address their long-term needs as they continue rebuilding their lives after years of abuse.You use AI every day. articles.title: A tropical system is likely in the Gulf this week despite El Niño. Here are the latest scenarios
articles.summary: An Atlantic hurricane season squashed by El Niño could come to life.
articles.body: A tropical depression or storm has a high chance to form in the Gulf this week and breathe life into the tail end of an Atlantic hurricane season squashed by El Niño. The Gulf is often a hot bed for late-season storms. Right on cue, chances are increasing for an area of stormy weather festering in the Gulf’s Bay of Campeche to spin up into one by midweek, according to the National Hurricane Center. The next storm name in the Atlantic is Isaias (ees-ah-EE-ahs). Exactly where the storm could track or how strong it could get is still up in the air. Gulf water is record warm for this time of year, primed to generate and help strengthen any system. But this potential storm’s overall strength could be capped by less favorable conditions in the atmosphere. No matter its final fate, heavy rain is a concern on the Gulf Coast and in other parts of the South by late this week. The forecast scenarios All three scenarios are still possible, but it’s looking more likely that a tropical system will form for at least some period of time. As this year has already shown, it doesn’t take a hurricane-strength system to cause significant impacts, particularly in a warming world that’s making tropical systems wetter. Tropical storms Arthur and Edouard didn’t last long, but their heavy rain resulted in significant flash flooding and water rescues. Parts of Louisiana and Mississippi took the brunt of Arthur’s flooding while Edouard dropped over 20 inches of rain in eastern Texas. Parts of Alabama, Georgia, the Florida Panhandle, southeast Louisiana and Mississippi are most at risk of heavy rain from this system. The downpours could start to ramp up along the coast as soon as Friday and then continue to soak the region while creeping farther inland through the weekend. Several inches of rain could fall, but it’s too soon to pinpoint which locations might see the most and could experience flash flooding. What’s typical in October and November Four named storms — that’s tropical storm strength or greater — typically form in October and November, but some hurricane seasons can have a stronger finish while others quiet down. The last few years illustrate this year-to-year ebb and flow. Seven storms formed during October and November in 2024, but just two formed during the same time in 2023. Late-season storms tend to form closer to the United States, including in the Gulf, Caribbean and off the Southeast coast, which makes them more likely to impact land. While there are usually fewer storms, they can still be destructive. Last year, Category 5 Hurricane Melissa devastated Jamaica in October’s final week. Hurricane Michael roared into the Florida Panhandle on October 10, 2018, becoming the latest landfalling Category 5 on record in the US. And Hurricane Sandy may be the most notorious of all: It morphed into a hybrid superstorm in late-October 2012 and walloped the East Coast. Super El Niño’s grip on the Atlantic basin means a repeat of notorious late-season hurricanes is less likely this year. Its storm-killing wind is the main reason this season could go hurricane-free for the first time in reliable records.

articles.title: Alleged Flydubai hijacker likely wanted to target Israel’s Ben Gurion Airport, sources say
articles.summary: The alleged hijacker of the Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv likely wanted to target Israel’s Ben Gurion Airport, the country’s main international gateway, according to an Israeli official and an Israeli source familiar with the matter.
articles.body: The alleged hijacker of the Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv likely wanted to target Israel’s Ben Gurion Airport, the country’s main international gateway, according to an Israeli official and an Israeli source familiar with the matter. Hamam al-Hammami, the suspect in the hijacking attempt and co-pilot on board the flight, was stopped by the actions of the captain and several passengers who restrained him and wrested control of the airplane. The official and the source said Israel is receiving updates from the Emiratis and that the investigation was still in its early stages. There are still questions about the suspect’s intentions, they added. Israel’s Channel 12 News first reported that Tel Aviv’s Ben Gurion Airport may have been the target of the hijacking. It’s unclear why al-Hammami allegedly attacked the captain, Smit Machchhar, over Saudi airspace if his goal was to target an airport in Israel. When Israel detected an inbound commercial jet signaling a potential hijacking on September 30, authorities there scrambled Israeli fighter jets as a precaution – standard procedure for such an emergency scenario. The United Arab Emirates is leading the investigation into the attempted hijacking on board Flydubai’s FZ1073 to learn the motives behind the attack and understand how the suspect was able to get through the safeguards of two countries known for their strict security protocols. Israel’s Tax Authority confirmed the names of all passengers and crew were in the hands of Israeli authorities before the flight had taken off, but it said questions about the vetting of crew members should be referred to the Ministry of Transport. Shin Bet, Israel’s internal security agency, also referred CNN to the Ministry of Transport, which it said is “responsible for all security matters concerning foreign airlines.” The Ministry of Transport said that its procedures do not include checking the names of flight crew members, although those names are submitted to the Israel Tax Authority, which collects them in case of requests by security services. The ministry added that all flight crew members are required to have a travel visa to enter the country, and an Omani passport should have been flagged at check-in. But the ministry also said its “procedures do not address the threat from a pilot.” Suspect likely acted alone CNN reported on Sunday that the suspect probably acted alone, and Israel is so far not aware of a link to any terrorist organization that trained, funded, or organized the attack. The attorney general of the UAE, Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, said the co-pilot on board the flight had attempted to seize control of the plane by attacking his colleague with a crash ax – a piece of equipment required on most aircraft. The attorney general called the attempted hijacking a “terrorist act.” The suspect, al-Hammami, had been removed from his previous job at Oman’s national airline on the track to be a pilot following concerns about his extremist views, sources told CNN earlier. He was moved to a desk job at the company, one of the sources said. Flydubai said it couldn’t comment on the matter while an investigation was underway. CNN has also reached out to Oman Air, the UAE Foreign Ministry and the Dubai government’s media office for comment. Aviation experts have told CNN that when it comes to vetting pilots, the responsibility lies with local governments, airlines and security services. Experts said pilots’ licenses and security passes are handled at the national level, and the rules vary depending on the country.

articles.title: Trump’s senior moment turns Brazil into India
articles.summary: TOI correspondent from Washington: At 60, confusing Brazil with India would be a gaffe.
articles.body: TOI correspondent from Washington: At 60, confusing Brazil with India would be a gaffe. At 80, it’s seen as going ga-ga -- or to put it kindly, having a “senior moment.”US President Donald Trump, not known for his mastery of geography or history while claiming infallible memory and knowledge, blew it again on Sunday when he mistakenly posted about a purported election in India, when it was actually Brazil that went to the polls.“125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the SAME DAY! In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate,” Trump posted shortly before midnight, using a foreign prop to complain that elections in America are corrupt – unless, as critics have pointed out, he wins, in which case it's fine.Trump later corrected the error, but the horse, or post, had bolted, with social media doing the rest. The original was screenshotted, reposted, mocked and converted into political ammunition before the correction could catch up.For a president who has made a political capital out of branding other people's verbal slips as evidence of incompetence, the episode was cannon fodder for his critics. And because Trump is now 80, an age at which every stumble, lapse, squint and misplaced noun is examined under a political microscope, it immediately became more than a geographical gaffe; it became gold dust for geriatric gags.“Grandpa really needs to sleep at night,” one wag weighed in, referring to Trump’s increasingly nocturnal social media forays where, even some of his supporters concede, he posts “batshit crazy stuff.”There is also a growing industry in schadenfreude -- the joy or pleasure of witnessing someone’s humiliation or embarrassment, given that Trump has spent years weaponising age and mental acuity against his political opponents, notably calling his predecessor Joe Biden “Sleepy Joe” and portraying himself as a vigorous replacement.But his own verbal miscues are accumulating by the day, and his rather elastic relationship with the geography of America's neighbours and the wider world has become a butt of jokes. From inventing a country called “Nambia” to mispronouncing Nepal as “nipple” and Bhutan as “button,” and believing they are part of India, to coveting Canada and Greenland and calling Belgium a "beautiful city," he has crushed cartography.The India-Brazil episode is particularly awkward because it involved two of the world's largest democracies on opposite sides of the world, they are both members of BRICS which the MAGA boss dislikes, and a presidential election had occurred literally the previous day in a hemisphere Trump wants the US to dominate.The irony is that Trump does not behave like a man eager to retire into the Florida sunshine. He remains arguably the most visible president in US history, constantly traveling, playing golf, holding rallies, speaking extemporaneously for long periods, posting at all hours and routinely subjecting himself to the peculiar punishment of the modern presidency: standing before cameras and microphones while the entire world watches.On the other side of the ledger is what his critics increasingly describe as a catalogue of physical signs of aging. He has repeatedly been photographed with his eyes closed during meetings and public events. When asked about one particularly conspicuous episode during a Cabinet meeting, he rejected the suggestion that he had fallen asleep, explaining that he was merely bored, “I didn't sleep,” he said. “I just closed them because I wanted to get the hell out of here.”Trump's approach to health, age, and geography provides plenty of material for the comedians without requiring any help from his enemies. At an event over the weekend in Ohio, where he was campaigning for Vivek Ramaswamy, he volunteered a new chapter in his long-running aspirin saga, disclosing that he takes a mega dose of Bayer aspirin every day because he needs it psychologically. Meanwhile, Brazil, India, and many other countries in the world are reaching for something stronger to take care of the headaches he is causing.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Divers found a 400-year-old shipwreck while clearing a German gas pipeline route; two anchors, woodworking tools and a mystery brick survived in the silt
articles.summary: Divers sent to clear dangerous metal from a planned gas pipeline route in Germany's Bay of Greifswald expected to find only modern debris and wartime
articles.body: Divers sent to clear dangerous metal from a planned gas pipeline route in Germany's Bay of Greifswald expected to find only modern debris and wartime leftovers. Instead, in 2023, they pulled up shoe soles, wooden pulley blocks and an iron anchor from a seventeenth-century ship. Underwater archaeologist Michał Konrad Grabowski describes the discovery in a preliminary report in the International Journal of Nautical Archaeology, published by Taylor and Francis. The rescue team had only twelve days before dredging began, yet it recovered more than sixty objects, including one baffling brick-like item that still has no explanation.A routine search for dangerous seabed objects before gas pipeline construction uncovered a lost shipAccording to Grabowski's report, the find began with the Ostsee Anbindungsleitung project. It is a fifty-kilometre underwater gas pipeline linking a new liquefied natural gas terminal at Mukran, on the island of Rügen, with a gas transmission facility near the seaside resort of Lubmin. Before building, crews must neutralise hazardous objects on the seabed, such as unexploded wartime munitions and metal debris, and an archaeological watching brief usually accompanies this work.About three kilometres north of Lubmin, clearance divers investigated a cluster of magnetic anomalies. They brought up wooden blocks, rigging, leather shoe soles and a large stock anchor with its wooden stock still attached. Work stopped immediately, and the state heritage authority for Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania was notified. The finds were kept in wet storage to prevent drying out, and a full archaeological campaign began in early July 2023.How divers raced the dredging schedule to record the wreckThe team made twenty-two dives over twelve days. The divers were a mix of commercial divers and maritime archaeologists, working from a thirty-metre vessel with surface-supplied air and radio communication. Their positions were tracked in real time and combined with magnetic, sonar and photographic survey data.The wreck lay at an average depth of seven and a half metres, almost entirely buried in soft, fine silt. Even slight disturbance clouded the water, so visibility was poor. The first large timbers appeared only half a metre below the seabed, and most objects lay between half a metre and one metre underground, scattered and disconnected.What survives of this seventeenth-century hullThe largest surviving piece of hull measures roughly seven and a half metres by one metre. It has five overlapping planks and a few frames, and Grabowski identified it as part of the rear starboard side. The planks are about four centimetres thick and overlap in the clinker style, like roof shingles. They were fastened with iron nails and sealed with a mixture of tar and animal hair. The frame arrangement is consistent with a shell-first building method, in which the outer planking is assembled before the internal frames.One striking object is a bilge pump tube, hollowed from a single oak trunk and about 3.6 metres long. By comparing it with other Baltic wrecks, Grabowski tentatively estimated a vessel of nineteen to twenty-two metres in length, six to seven metres in width and about three metres in internal depth. He stresses that this is conjecture, because so little of the hull survives.Anchors, rigging blocks, a grindstone and woodworking tools suggest a ship prepared for long voyagesThe two wrought-iron stock anchors are very similar, with shanks of about 1.8 metres and wooden stocks of about 2.2 metres. They may be a matched pair of bow anchors. Nearby lay a solid pine buoy, probably used to mark an anchor's position, and a similar buoy was found on the Swedish warship Vasa.The rigging finds include single-sheave wooden blocks, mostly of ash, along with deadeyes and heart blocks. A grindstone about thirty centimetres across and several carpentry tools point to an onboard workshop, which Grabowski links to long-distance merchant ships or warships. The hand brace handle closely resembles examples from the Tudor warship Mary Rose. Nearly all the tools came from one magnetic anomaly, together with barrel staves and what may be spare iron fasteners stored in casks.The pierced clay brick in an oak housing remains an unexplained objectThe most puzzling find is a flat fragment of fine yellowish clay brick, about thirteen by seven centimetres and three centimetres thick. It is pierced by four cone-shaped holes, with part of a fifth, and is fitted tightly into an oak housing about fifteen by twelve centimetres. Grabowski found no direct parallels anywhere.His cautious suggestion is a sharpening device for drill bits or chisels, possibly made from a damaged tool and remounted in a new wooden frame. Until a match turns up, the object remains the wreck's central mystery.Dating the wreck and glimpsing the crew's everyday life aboardFive oak samples went for tree-ring analysis. One plank gave a felling date between 1626 and 1639, and another was cut no earlier than 1615. The two datable samples matched different regions, one in north-eastern Germany between Stralsund and Güstrow and the other in southern Norway, so the ship's place of origin cannot be determined.Personal belongings are scarce. There are two shoe soles from two different pairs, one about twenty-three centimetres long and one about seventeen, plus a stitched leather strap. Six animal bones from pigs and sheep or goats hint at meals eaten on board.Why the ship sank is unknown; the Peene Strait shipping route is nearbySeveral timbers show signs of burning, which may point to a dramatic end. The two anchors and the buoy lay close together, suggesting the ship may have been deliberately anchored before it sank. About seven kilometres east lies the Peene Strait, the main route between the Oder estuary and the Baltic Sea until the late eighteenth century. An eighteenth-century Dutch sea chart shows anchorages nearby, the westernmost close to the wreck.Grabowski treats all of this as tentative. With no cargo and only a fragment of hull, the ship's name, origin, destination, and crew remain unknown.Test pits to the west found no further remains, so the pipeline trench was moved twenty-six metres southwest to avoid the wreck. Layers of sandbags covered the exposed timbers during construction, and divers re-examined the site in 2024 to check for damage. The seabed to the east has never been surveyed, so more of the ship may still lie buried there.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Cyklar is all over your feed, but is the viral body care brand actually worth buying? We tested it to find out
articles.summary: Cyklar is viral on social media, but is it worth the hefty price tag? Our NBC Selected editors tested its most popular products to find out what’s worth buying and skipping.
articles.body: I spend hours on self care TikTok, watching people share, for example, their shower essentials, how they’re layering fragrances and their ideal bedtime routines. Body care brand Cyklar pops up time and time again, specifically for its minimal, luxurious packaging and ultra-viral Vanilla Verve scent. But what makes Cyklar different from other body care brands, and does it actually live up to the hype? NBC Selected editors tested out the brand’s most popular products for two months to see if it’s worth adding to your cart. Below are our honest thoughts, including what surprised us, what we’d change and whether we’d actually recommend it. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. Our honest review of Cyklar Cyklar’s body cream is easily one of its most viral products, and we tried the brand’s most popular scents: Bergamot Bond, Naked Neroli, Sacred Santal, Rose Bud and Vanilla Verve. “I’m not much of a body lotion person, but if I have to use one, I prefer this one. It smells amazing but isn’t so potent that it feels like the scent is clogging my nostrils,” says NBC Selected associate social media editor Caitlin Cusack. The lotion is lightweight yet still quite hydrating. However, our editors agree this wouldn’t work for those who have extremely dry skin since it’s on the lighter side, especially during the colder months. Though the packaging looks chic and luxurious, it’s not much different from any other body lotion you have on your bathroom counter. “I appreciate the ingredients but I don’t think this lotion is anything to write home about. It doesn’t feel rich or elevated to me,” says Brown. “The consistency is on the lighter side and I feel like the package implies I’m going to get something different from what I expect, just based on looking at it.” This is a great product to use with another, more hydrating lotion, especially if you love smelling good all day. “It actually lasts longer than my perfume,” says NBC Selected editorial operations associate Jem Alabi. “That being said, this isn’t the most moisturizing. It’s a great option for the summer but I would use something thicker and less fragranced in the winter.” Perhaps the product that has come up the most on my For Your page (and likely yours too), this in-shower body oil makes your skin feel soft and smooth after your shower. You apply it after your typical shower routine while your skin is still wet and towel dry normally afterward. Truthfully, I didn’t know how to feel about it at first: Because it’s an oil balm, it felt slick and heavy when I applied it on my wet skin, almost like a film all over my body. “This may have my all-time favorite Hanni Splash Salve beat,” says NBC Selected senior editor Nikki Brown. “It really comes down to the application: It’s uncomplicated, and I simply rub it all over my damp skin and let it dry down. As long as you give the bottle a little shake beforehand, the product comes out evenly and goes smooth across the skin.” It dries down quickly, which lets you layer a lotion on top, too. But in Brown’s experience, it’s moisturizing enough to wear alone, especially if you’re in a rush or running late to work. As a beauty editor, I’ve tried hundreds of body washes, so it takes a lot to impress me. Cyklar’s Sensorial Body Wash actually blew me away. I have very dry skin, so some body washes tend to leave my skin feeling tight and stripped. This one feels like a large glass of water for my skin: It’s extremely lightweight, has a glorious gel-like texture and leaves my skin soft, smooth and hydrated. All of the scents, especially the vanilla and rose bud scents, stay on my skin all day long, too (however, they’re more on the subtle side, which I actually prefer). “I’m really picky with body washes: I like foaming formulas and can’t stand anything that leaves a residue on my skin. Luckily, this body wash ticks all my boxes,” says NBC Selected associate SEO reporter Ashley Morris. “The gel foams up easily once I add water, and the scent stays on my skin even after I’ve washed it off.” The pump packaging is also a huge plus because it’s easy to use with one hand and doesn’t leave a messy residue on the top. “It makes it so much easier to apply to my washcloth as opposed to a tube lid,” says Morris. Alabi specifically likes the Sacred Santal scent, which has notes of bergamot, cardamom, wood and vanilla. “It’s mature, sweet and perfectly balanced. I actually got compliments from my friends about how good I smelled and I wasn’t wearing any perfume,” she says. “I’ve tested over a dozen body oils, and this product is definitely in my top three,” says Cusack. It has a lightweight consistency that’s easy to blend in, plus a little goes a very long way. “It’s not sticky at all and doesn’t transfer to my clothes, even immediately after applying,” says Cusack. It also has vitamin C, which helps reduce hyperpigmentation and redness, and helps your skin produce more collagen, according to dermatologists we previously spoke to. “My favorite part is the scent I tried; I’m a vanilla girl, and this is one of the strongest vanilla-scented products I’ve ever tried — it’s the type of scent that will have people chasing you on the street to ask what you’re wearing.” (However, keep in mind the scent doesn’t last for more than a few hours.) I had used several milky toners on my face, so I was very intrigued to use one on my body, too. It’s not as hydrating as a lotion, which makes it a great option for the summer months when I don’t need as much hydration. However, I love using this before layering my favorite body lotion on top because it adds a boost of hydration that my dry skin usually needs. It’s fragrance-free, which makes it great for sensitive skin (though that’s another reason I use my favorite scented body lotion on top). The essence is extremely lightweight, so my skin drinks it right up and doesn’t leave a sticky or heavy residue. You can also use this semi-hydrating essence in place of a body lotion, according to Cusack. “I’m not a fan of smearing body lotion on because I have sensitive, acne-prone skin, and this product is a great alternative,” she says. It has a light, milky consistency that her skin absorbs quickly, so it doesn’t need any time to dry. “I used it after every shower for an entire week, and my skin felt softer, more hydrated and I even noticed less redness,” says Cusack. This ended up being NBC Selected reporter Zoe Malin’s favorite product she tried from Cyklar’s body care line. “I don’t normally use body scrubs, but this one convinced me that I should,” she says. “It turns my shower into a spa-like experience and feels like a genuine self care moment. I only need a little scrub to cover my body, and as I rub it in, the sandy texture quickly turns into an almost buttery feel.” Both Malin’s and my experience are the same after using it: After rinsing the scrub off, our skin is hydrated, soft, smooth and moisturized. “I kept touching my skin after I used it for the first time because I couldn’t believe how soft and smooth it was,” says Malin. Even though it’s exfoliating, it doesn’t irritate our sensitive skin at all. Plus, the tub packaging looks elevated and luxurious, so I love displaying it in my shower. The Sacred Santal scent is an NBC Selected editor-favorite, too. We’re constantly trying new exfoliating products to target texture and acne on our face and body, so we were pleasantly surprised when this one stood out across most of the products we’ve tested. “This is now my go-to product for my keratosis pilaris,” says Alabi. “It has a super fine mist, it isn’t greasy and rubs into my skin seamlessly. All other products I’ve used for my KP have been very drying, abrasive or I can only use in the shower, so this spray takes the crown.” Though the spray is meant to target rough texture or uneven skin tone, it can still be helpful for other concerns like acne and redness. “I get acne patches on my back after long runs that cause me to wear a super sweaty sports bra for hours. I’ve been applying this spray to my back and shoulders after showering post-long run and I think it’s helping with minor breakouts on my body,” says Malin. “It dries pretty quickly, so I don’t worry about the spray getting on clothes, and it’s not too harsh for my sensitive skin at all.” Our editors specifically love the spray bottle, which makes it easier to target any areas of your body when you’re applying it on yourself compared to a cream or serum, says Malin. It’s fragrance-free, too, which is key for people who may be prone to acne or irritation. Since the gel dries clear, it’s a great option if you hate seeing deodorant residue on your clothes. It also has mandelic acid, an alpha hydroxy acid that smooths texture and brightens skin. However, it’s not an antiperspirant, which means you’ll still sweat and likely have some odor to go along with it. After using it for a few days in the summer heat, there’s only so much the classic vanilla scent can cover up. And for a $20 deodorant, I’d rather put my money elsewhere. “As someone who leans more towards the sweatier side, deodorants are a strict subject in my eyes. Although I wouldn’t wear this formula for a heavy-duty workout, I do love that the scent is strong enough to make it seem as though I’m wearing perfume,” says Morris. “It’s a great everyday formula, both for the office and around the house, and I like that the gel dries down quickly once I apply it.” “I’m skeptical of most exfoliating body washes, however this one instantly intrigued me with its grainy texture. I definitely feel the beads on my skin, but they aren’t abrasive, which made it a better body scrub than straight exfoliant to me,” says Morris. While her skin felt smoother overall, Morris says she had to use quite a bit of product to achieve the foaming texture (which she looks for in a body wash). I’m a fan of the lactic acid in the formula since it helps reduce texture on my skin, which I tend to get on my legs and on the back of my arms. However, neither Morris nor I noticed a huge difference in the brightness of our skin. I also found the smell entirely off-putting; it smells vaguely like chemicals, and it definitely lingers after my shower. As their name suggests, each of these soaps has a rope at the end to avoid dropping it in the shower. The concept is basic, but it’s smart and effective, says Brown. “Soap is obviously slippery, so I love that this makes it way less likely to happen,” she says. Cyklar’s soap has an exfoliating blend of alpha hydroxy acids, volcanic pumice and polyhydroxy acids, so skin feels soft and smooth after you use it. “It has just enough microexfoliants to clean my skin without it feeling like sandpaper or worse, causing irritation. I can use this without a washcloth and still feel clean,” says Brown. Unlike Brown, who loves bar soap because she’s able to use it more mindfully than a body wash, Malin isn’t usually a bar soap person. “I was prepared to hate this, but I honestly didn’t,” says Malin. “It turned into a milky lather as I rubbed the bar against damp skin, and it noticeably exfoliates, but it’s not rough or irritating against my sensitive skin at all.” She hangs the bar up in her shower from the rope, so it dries between uses and doesn’t get gross and goopy. “I actually liked hanging it up better than putting it in the brand’s soap box, but I did think it was helpful when the bar was totally dry.” The biggest downside is that these soaps tend to leave colored residue on showers and tubs, making it much messier than a typical bar soap. For example, Malin, who tested the Cedar Supreme Soap, has orange marks on her shower walls after using it, and Brown, who tried the Lover’s Leather Soap, noticed black spots all over the shower. “That drives me nuts — I don’t want to have to clean my shower every time I use this soap, but I kind of have to,” says Malin. The brand’s Self-Tanning Milky Essence has a similar, lightweight texture to the original essence, but leaves a bronzed finish instead. “I’m a pale girl, so I’m always looking for a good self-tanner, even in the summer. This is the first tanning essence I’ve tried and was pleasantly surprised by how much I liked it,” says Cusack, “Because of the thin, milky consistency, it blended into my skin quickly and didn’t leave any residue.” Cusack was impressed with the overall look of the tan, which took about six hours to develop and made her skin look glowy and bronzed. “I even got a few compliments on how good my tan looked,” she says. However, it still has the strong self-tanner smell, which Cusack says lingered for about a day. “I’ve had the vanilla version of this hand cream for over a month now, and I never leave the house without at least one of them in my bag,” says Morris. It has a thicker, creamy texture that keeps hands hydrated (even on chillier days), and it absorbs quickly, so you don’t have an uncomfortable, heavy feel on your hands afterward. Plus, it has urea, which softens and hydrates skin. Our only issue is that the tube is too big to fit in some of our smaller purses and bags, which is where we usually store our hand creams. As a big fan of smelling good at all times, I carry small travel-sized fragrances and perfume oils wherever I go. When I first received this perfume oil set from the brand, I was impressed by how gorgeous the packaging was. It comes in a briefcase-style gift box that opens to reveal eight scents: Sacred Santal, Vanilla Verve, Sex Musk, Flora Veil, Modern Patchouli, Lover’s Leather, Cedar Supreme and Bergamot Bond (many of which, unfortunately, aren’t yet available as scents in most of their body care collection). Each perfume oil fits comfortably in any purse or bag I own, and since a little goes a long way, they last a very long time. In fact, I’ve had these oils for over a year, and I’m only halfway done with most of them. When it comes to a specific roll-on scent, Vanilla Verve is a favorite among our editors. “The brand sent me a sample of this a while ago. It’s the perfect balance of vanilla mixed with a powerful woody smell that I love,” says NBC Selected commerce editor Cory Fernandez. “I enjoy vanilla scents, but not when they’re sugary; this one is perfectly neutral. Also, since it’s a roll-on, a little goes a long way and the scent is strong in the best way.” What can improve Though we think Cyklar is, in fact, worth the hype for most of its products, there are a few downsides to keep in mind: Products are pricey: Most of Cyklar’s body care products, including its body lotion, body wash and essences, cost upwards of $30, which is typically a lot for everyday basics. Some products, namely the Nutrient-Rich Body Cream and the Lactic Acid Foaming Body Polish, aren’t worth the price tag simply because they don’t quite deliver on their promises or have cheaper, better alternatives. Polarizing scents: Scents are extremely subjective, so not every fragrance is going to satisfy every person. Cyklar is known for having woody and earthy scents like bergamot and santal, which aren’t what many people lean toward when it comes to everyday body care. However, the scent options have been growing and continue to grow, which gives pickier people a chance to find one that works for them.Not for very dry skin: Cyklar has several products aimed at hydrating and nourishing skin, but our editors agree that most simply don’t hit the mark for people with very dry skin. Most of the products are light and semi-hydrating, which is great for the hotter, summer months, but don’t quite cut it for the winter. How we tested Cyklar body care Six editors tested over a dozen of Cyklar’s body care products for three months. The products were across categories, including body lotions, hand creams, body washes, self-tanners and more, with each editor keeping their individual skin care concerns in mind, including dryness, acne and texture. When testing, we used each product based on the brand’s instructions and kept the following factors in mind: Texture and application: How does the product feel on skin? Is it easy to apply? Does it feel gentle or harsh while applying it?Effectiveness: What is the product’s intended purpose and did it deliver on its promise? Did we note any negative side effects, like breakouts, irritation or redness?Scent: Does it have a noticeable fragrance? If so, was it strong or subtle? How long did it last, and did it fade quickly?Skin concerns: Did it help improve skin concerns like texture and breakouts? Is it suitable for sensitive skin?Packaging: Does it come in a pump, tube or jar? Is it easy to use/dispense? Is the packaging travel-friendly?Value: Is the product size and feel worth the money? Would you repurchase it? Who is Cyklar for? If you’re a fan of luxurious packaging and fancy scents for your body care, Cyklar is definitely a brand worth considering. It looks fantastic on a bathroom counter or shower, and the scents for the creams and body washes generally last for several hours, according to our editors. The products also have ingredients that are backed by dermatologists we’ve spoken to in the past, including ceramides, ectoin, glycerin and vitamin C. If you have very dry skin, you might want to consider layering these products with more hydrating creams, lotions and oils in the winter (or skipping out altogether based on the price). You also might want to steer clear of most of the brand’s creams if you’re sensitive to fragrance since there are limited fragrance-free options (though they do exist for some products, like the Glycolic Acid Exfoliating Body Spray and Ceramide Milky Essence). If you’re looking for a more hydrating (and cheaper) alternative to Cyklar’s viral body cream, consider the Cerave Moisturizing Face & Body Cream ($15.99), Gold Bond Healing Sensitive Daily Body & Face Lotion ($9.99) and La Roche-Posay Lipikar AP+MAX Triple Repair Moisturizing Body Cream ($22.99). If you’re looking for one that’s more affordable and smells equally amazing, try the Eos Shea Better Body Lotion in Vanilla Cashmere ($10.99), which is my personal favorite. Why trust NBC Selected? I’m a commerce editor at NBC Selected who has covered beauty, skin care, hair care and wellness for more than six years. I’ve also tested hundreds of skin and body care products to find the best ones worth buying. For this article, five editors and I tested Cyklar’s popular body care products and rounded up our honest thoughts about each one. Catch up on NBC Selected’s in-depth coverage of tech and tools, wellness and more, and follow us on Facebook, Instagram, X and TikTok to stay up to date.

articles.title: 'American Idol' alum Caleb Flynn weeps as daughters ask him why he killed their mother, vow not to visit him
articles.summary: Caleb Flynn was sentenced to life without parole, plus 16 years, after an Ohio jury convicted the former "American Idol" contestant of murdering his wife.
articles.body: Former "American Idol" contestant Caleb Flynn was sentenced Monday to life without the possibility of parole for murdering his wife, with an Ohio judge ordering him to first serve 16 additional years behind bars. Miami County Judge Jeannine N. Pratt ordered Flynn to serve seven years for firearm specifications followed by nine years for three counts of tampering with evidence before beginning his life sentence for the murder of Ashley Flynn. Pratt said consecutive sentences were necessary to protect the public and punish Flynn, finding the harm caused by his crimes was so severe that a single prison term would not adequately reflect the seriousness of his conduct. 'AMERICAN IDOL' ALUM CALEB FLYNN CONVICTED OF MURDERING HIS WIFE Before Flynn was sentenced, one of his daughters confronted him in a letter read aloud in court by her uncle, Matthew Keyt. "How could you do such a thing? I looked up to you. I loved you with all my heart," Flynn's daughter wrote. "Mommy was the perfect person. The absolute perfect person. What did she ever do to make you hate her so much?" She wrote that she cries every day over her mother's death but still prays every night for her father to confess and repent. "It was your choice to have an affair. It was your choice to lie to everyone," she wrote. "It was your choice to leave your only two daughters." CALEB FLYNN'S LOVE SONGS TO MISTRESS PLAYED IN COURT AS RELATIVES AWKWARDLY LOOK ON Flynn's other daughter, Alyssa, also confronted her father in a letter read aloud by her grandmother, Jill Smith. "The least you could do is tell everyone you did it and receive your outcome," Alyssa wrote. "Also, please repent to God, the one who created you. Your time isn't over." WATCH: Letter from Caleb Flynn's daughter read in court before sentencing Alyssa questioned how her father could stand in church and sing about his love for God while keeping secrets from his family, and told him Ashley was "the best thing that ever happened to you." "Through all of what you put me through, God is going to work something out for good," Alyssa wrote. "And by the way, I don't plan on coming to see you." As his daughter's words were read aloud, Flynn could be heard sobbing into a tissue at the defense table. Ashley's sister, Kayla Keyt, also addressed Flynn directly, telling him he had taken a mother from her daughters and shattered a family that trusted him. DAD OF 'AMERICAN IDOL' CONTESTANT'S SLAIN WIFE MADE EERIE GOOGLE SEARCH AFTER HEARING OF HER MURDER "You took Ashley from the earth," Keyt said. "You took a mother from her daughters." Keyt told Flynn she nevertheless forgave him, saying she refused to allow hatred and bitterness to take anything else from her family. WATCH: Ashley Flynn's sister rips her killer Caleb Flynn Flynn addressed the court before sentencing, saying it was his first opportunity to speak publicly in eight months. He first addressed his daughters, telling them they remained his "greatest joy" and apologizing for the milestones he would miss. Flynn later apologized to Ashley's family for breaking his marriage vows and for the pain caused by his decisions, saying he took responsibility for his words and actions. But he stopped short of accepting responsibility for Ashley's murder. "I did not kill my wife," Flynn said, adding that he would continue fighting to prove his innocence. Flynn received credit for 229 days already spent in jail and was ordered to pay $20,000 in restitution for funeral expenses, along with court costs. Jurors found Flynn guilty of aggravated murder, three counts of murder, two counts of felonious assault and three counts of tampering with evidence after roughly 2½ hours of deliberations. His defense argued that Flynn has no prior criminal history and is capable of rehabilitation, pointing to his years working in ministry and letters of support from his family. Flynn's parents were among several relatives who wrote to Pratt asking for mercy ahead of sentencing. His father, Mike Flynn, told the judge his son's "brokenness, shame, and remorse" were genuine, while his mother, Kim Flynn, wrote that her son had "repented to his Lord" and was remorseful for his decisions. Both asked Pratt for mercy. Prosecutors sharply disputed that portrayal, arguing Flynn has never accepted responsibility or shown genuine remorse. They are asking Pratt to sentence him to life without the possibility of parole. FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X The verdict capped a trial that exposed Flynn's secret affair, thousands of messages with his mistress and exchanges about wanting his wife dead before she was shot twice in the back of the head inside the couple's Tipp City home Feb. 16. Prosecutors argued Flynn killed Ashley before staging the scene to make it appear an intruder had broken into the home. Flynn's affair with Alleigha Botner became a key part of the case. Investigators recovered roughly 107,000 messages between the two, with prosecutors highlighting some of those exchanges for jurors. SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS Jurors saw messages in which Flynn discussed wanting his wife dead and contemplated ways she could be killed without him going to prison. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB Botner also read messages exchanged in the hours before Ashley's death, including Flynn telling her, "It's happening" and "Tomorrow it all starts." In another exchange, Botner told Flynn, "You're about to be free." SEND US A TIP Flynn's defense argued the messages were being taken out of context and that references to being "free" meant divorce rather than murder. GOT A TIP? Investigators never recovered the murder weapon, and Flynn was never tested for gunshot residue. LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST Jurors heard testimony about searches of storm drains, culverts, the Flynn home and other locations as investigators tried unsuccessfully to find the gun. articles.title: What is ‘Herod’s Pool’, and why is Israel developing it in the West Bank?
articles.summary: Israel is developing a reservoir on land in the occupied West Bank, with water syphoned off from Palestinians.
articles.body:
Israel says that work has begun on a development project around an outdoor pool in the occupied West Bank filled after settlers illegally diverted water from a Palestinian village over the summer.

Instead of restoring the water to the village of Fasayil, near Jericho, Israeli authorities are working to formalise what has now been termed “Herod’s Pool”, named after an ancient Jewish king.

On Sunday, Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, a far-right settler, announced that “development and preservation” of Herod’s Pool had commenced, connecting it to a larger project to “strengthen [Israel’s] hold” on and preserve historical sites.

“The Settlement Revolution continues!” he declared in a social media post that carried an image of workers and wheelbarrows near the site.

The announcement follows Smotrich’s June pledge of more than three million shekels (almost $1m) to develop the site, even though the pool sits on privately-owned Palestinian land belonging to a farmer.

The illegal diversion of water to the pool is part of Israel’s monopolisation of water resources in the occupied West Bank’s fertile Jordan Valley.

It also marks the latest Israeli seizure of Palestinian land in the name of archaeological heritage.

Here’s what we know about the Herod’s Pool project.

Herod’s Pool is the name Israeli settlers have given an ancient reservoir that lies in the Palestinian village of Fasayil. It is named after Herod the Great, a Jewish king from the first century BC.

The reservoir sits next to a natural spring.

Although settlers claim it once belonged to King Herod, archaeologists have not established when the pool was built. Alon Arad, executive director of Emek Shaveh, an Israeli NGO that defends cultural heritage rights and monitors the political use of archaeology, told the Reuters news agency that the pool’s origins are unclear.

“We see in many cases the use of archaeology … to create this feeling that the West Bank is exclusively Jewish,” he said.

Israeli politicians and settlers have also sought greater Israeli control over “Solomon’s Pools”, three ancient reservoirs in Bethlehem governorate, which have been used by Palestinians for generations.

Palestinians say the targeting of their water sources is part of a comprehensive plan to seize the resources of the occupied West Bank and force them off their land.

The reservoir sits on land belonging to Palestinian farmer Saad Nemer and his family. Nemer says that his grandfather purchased the property more than a century ago. Israeli-issued documentation and older title records reviewed by Reuters support the family’s ownership claim.

Nemer said that settlers had been repeatedly redirecting water from his farm to swim in the pool. He explained that settlers had stolen his irrigation pipeline for the task, and over time the theft had left his farmland scorched and his greenhouses empty.

Nemer also said that settlers had threatened him and beat one of his employees.

The Israeli military body that administers the occupied West Bank, COGAT, has acknowledged that the water was diverted “without authorisation” and said it would investigate, even as Smotrich and other Israeli politicians celebrate the pool.

Nemer told The New York Times that he had been informed by COGAT that his water would be restored, but said it returned for only one day before being cut off again. He is now fearful of approaching the reservoir to reconnect his pipeline due to settler violence.

How have Israeli settlers invoked Herod?

While there is no proven link to Herod, the name features prominently in Israeli heritage projects across the occupied West Bank , which Israel refers to as “Judea and Samaria” in an attempt to separate it from its Palestinian population.

Critics, including archaeological rights groups, say such projects are increasingly being used to extend Israeli control over Palestinian land and heritage sites.

There is Herodium, a sprawling hilltop structure south of Jerusalem, said to be the ruins of a fortress the king erected. It has been under Israeli control for decades and operates as a national park, despite Palestinian protests that it is part of their heritage.

In Sebastia – ancient Samaria – Israel has dedicated large amounts of funding since 2023 to excavate the city’s archaeological park and develop it as an Israeli “ national park “, usurping Palestinians who have long showcased the archaeological ruins as part of their history.

Israeli Minister of Heritage Amichai Eliyahu, who himself lives in an illegal West Bank settlement, has said it would be “first and foremost a Jewish heritage site”. His office cited excavation of “the magnificent Roman city built by King Herod” when describing the archaeological periods the project intends to expose.

The Ibrahimi Mosque in Hebron – where Israel has repeatedly restricted Muslim access – stands on land considered to be Prophet Abraham’s burial place by Muslims and Jews. Part of it is believed to have been built during the Herodian era.

In 2017, UNESCO recognised Hebron’s Old City as a Palestinian heritage site, and warned that it was endangered by Israeli settler encroachments.

Ahead of UNESCO’s decision, prominent Hebron settler Yishai Fleisher – who has served as an adviser to Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir – objected to the designation on the grounds that it was “built by a Jewish king”, referring to Herod.

articles.title: What prompted the US bombers to leave RAF Fairford?
articles.summary: The mass evacuation of American bombers from the UK points to concern in the Pentagon, our security correspondent writes.
articles.body:
The unexpected mass withdrawal of America's heavy bombers happened so suddenly on Sunday that it has got everyone wondering what prompted it.

An "abundance of caution," says US Vice-President JD Vance, adding that Washington felt Iran was doing what it has "done for 49 years... which is engage in acts of terrorism against the US and against a lot of other people".

An abundance of panic is how others have seen it.

For the last seven months, America's B-1 Lancer bombers and other aircraft have been operating out of Fairford to strike the Iranian missile launch sites.

In July, Iran threatened any country that provided the US with such a facility would be considered a "legitimate target".

Then on 27 September, a major incident was declared when five British men were arrested and later bailed after being seen acting suspiciously with their three white vans in the dead of night close to the airbase perimeter.

At the weekend, a UK-Iranian dual national was arrested on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts. He was also released on bail.

Twelve valuable and strategically important B-1 bombers have now departed en masse and seemingly in such a rush that, reportedly, the air-to-air refuelling aircraft needed to get them back across the Atlantic to their home bases in the continental US were still being fuelled up while the B-1 Lancer crews were being ordered to scramble to take off.

So something was considered urgent and dangerous enough to prompt this.

Speaking after his vice-president's remarks, President Donald Trump himself said the US had removed its bombers because of "some threats" to the base.

"Rather than tempting the enemy", he added, the US had moved the planes "around a little bit".

There was almost certainly a fresh piece of intelligence, whether true or not.

British officials would not reveal what it was, but they did say "there is an ongoing high tempo of threat from Iran to the UK, and it is logical that US airbases would be pretty high on any targeting list".

Iran has denied any connection with events at RAF Fairford. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has also played down any suggested link between this rushed evacuation and the arrests made on 27 September.

The context here is that while the UK is not at war with Iran, the US is - and that is a distinction Tehran has publicly challenged. As far as the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps is concerned, Britain is already a participant in America's war with Iran.

There is also a cost factor involved here.

The B-1 Lancer bombers which have now left each cost about $330 million.

The Americans have already suffered heavy financial losses from Iranian strikes on US bases in the Middle East.

In late March the Iranians hit Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia, destroying an E-3 Sentry Awacs early warning plane.

That aircraft alone cost over half a billion dollars.

General Sir Richard Barrons, who served in one of the highest ranks in the British Armed Forces, said: "We now live in a world where a £1,000 drone could wreck one of those aircraft.

"So, I don't know what the threat was but the most prudent thing to do would be to remove them to Texas given that they were not doing very much at the minute."

Trump says 'threat' led US to pull bombers from RAF Fairford

No 10 insists RAF Fairford is safe after US withdraws bombers

What makes RAF Fairford one of the UK's most important military sites?

Peace for villagers as US bombers leave UK airbase

But how does the US ordering the bombers to leave RAF Fairford reflect on Washington's confidence in the ability of the UK to keep the base secure?

Britain remains an incredibly close ally of the US and there are still hundreds of American servicemen and women stationed at RAF Fairford, as well as at other bases at Mildenhall and Lakenheath.

Work will likely be ongoing in secret now to review security at the base on both sides of the perimeter fence.

But it is hard not to conclude that, despite efforts to play down the drama, this is an embarrassing episode for the UK.

Rubio said the US has "confidence in the security of all our bases" and said the administrations was working "very closely" with UK authorities, who "couldn't be more co-operative".

UK counter-terrorism police are still investigating what happened at RAF Fairford and are keeping an open mind as to what exactly was behind events there.

I have been told a large amount of data, CCTV and other information is still being trawled through while the men remain on bail.

Meanwhile, now that the bombers have left British soil, the US insists it can still deploy them from its domestic bases anywhere in the world.

That could be seen as putting a brave face on something which, for Iran, sees a major US strike force effectively driven back to its home base in the continental United States.

articles.title: An Arkansas gem hunter found a 6.03-carat yellow diamond after paying $15 to search a state park; he says it could be worth $1 million, but another appraisal puts it closer to $250,000
articles.summary: Jack Pearadin, a Navy reservist originally from Missouri, has been hunting diamonds at Arkansas’ Crater of Diamonds State Park since 2013.
articles.body: Jack Pearadin, a Navy reservist originally from Missouri, has been hunting diamonds at Arkansas’ Crater of Diamonds State Park since 2013. Over the years, he has unearthed more than 300 gems. But this time, when his shovel hit the gravel, he spotted something different. After rinsing the gravel and tipping it onto a table, he noticed a yellow crystal about the size of a fingernail catching the light. His TikTok livestream was still on, and this rock was a 6.03-carat diamond!‘Oh my God! Oh my God!’ Pearadin said during the livestream. ‘Holy cr*p, we got a big one!’ he yelled.It turns out it is the largest diamond found this year at Crater of Diamonds State Park in Arkansas. For Pearadin, it is unlike anything he has dug up before. Talking to the AP, he claimed the diamond could be worth $1 million.A hobby that is yet to pay offGem hunting may seem like a rewarding career. But Pearadin is the first to admit his hobby has not paid off. Over a dozen years, he has sifted through the rocks, and the field where this stone turned up has already given him more than 300 gems.Originally from Missouri, he first tried his luck at the park in 2013 and later moved to nearby Murfreesboro to stay close to it. ‘I love it that much,’ he told the outlet. Most of the diamonds he found were sold online.This one came out of the ground with help. Pearadin and his friend Michael Schumacher of Wisconsin shovelled it from the field together, and Schumacher helped fill the bucket that held the stone. Pearadin has named the diamond the ‘American Dream’.A diamond worth $1 millionPearadin thinks this new diamond he unearthed would fetch him $1 million. At least, that’s what some of the collectors told him. Appraisers are more cautious. At least one experienced appraiser told the news agency that a stone of this size and quality might be worth a quarter of that.Laura Stanley, a certified gem appraiser in Little Rock, said a high-quality six-carat yellow diamond from the park can sell for about $250,000. According to her, the park’s name is part of the reason. ‘They are their own entity. It’s the only place in America where you can go find your own diamond and you can’t compare that to a diamond from anywhere else,’ Stanley said.For some context, a typical 0.17-carat diamond from the park sells for around $700, Stanley said.Cutting will change the stone, too. Natural diamonds tend to be cloudy and oddly shaped, and they lose about 25% of their weight when cut and polished, Nathan Renfro, senior manager at the Gemological Institute of America, told AP.A $15 fee to find diamondsThe park charges $15 to fill a five-gallon bucket with rocks, and visitors keep any gemstones they find. Most of these finds are small and worth maybe a few hundred dollars. More than 37,000 diamonds have been discovered by gem hunters since the former open-pit mine became a state park in 1972.In a year, usually about 400 to 800 diamonds turn up, and most weigh about a quarter of a carat, according to park interpreter Sarah Bivens. Bigger ones are rare. Park assistant superintendent Waymon Cox revealed that a nine-carat diamond was found in 2020 by an Arkansas bank manager and a seven-carat stone was unearthed in 2024 by a French man.The biggest record belongs to Uncle Sam, a 40.23-carat crystal found in 1924, the largest diamond ever unearthed in the United States. It was cut into a 12.42-carat gem and gifted to the Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History, where it hangs in the ‘Great American Diamonds’ exhibit.Today, Arkansas’ park is one of the only places in the world where anyone can hunt for diamonds and take their finds with them. ‘It’s a pretty remarkable operation that that’s available to the public,’ Renfro said. ‘Most diamond mines are super high security.’Pearadin, on the other hand, has named his latest find the ‘American Dream’. ‘It’s just this massive, gorgeous yellow diamond,’ he said. The seasoned gem hunter plans to split the profits with his fellow hunter, Michael Schumacher of Wisconsin.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Euro slides to 17-month low, boosting dollar’s standing
articles.summary: The value of the euro slid on Monday to a 17-month low amid mounting government debt across Europe. As of mid-afternoon on the East Coast, one euro is worth roughly $1.12, after sinking below that threshold earlier in the day. The European currency hit its lowest point since May 2025, when it was roughly equivalent…
articles.body:
The value of the euro slid on Monday to a 17-month low amid mounting government debt across Europe.

As of mid-afternoon on the East Coast, one euro is worth roughly $1.12 , after sinking below that threshold earlier in the day. The European currency hit its lowest point since May 2025, when it was roughly equivalent to $1.11.

At the start of the year, the euro was worth roughly $1.17. As recently as mid-September, it was worth more than $1.16.

The value of the euro has not dipped below $1 since November 2022, when it was below that mark for roughly six weeks . That marked the first time it was worth less than $1 in about two decades.

A weakening euro strengthens the U.S. dollar in comparison, making European exports cheaper. A stronger dollar relative to the euro could make American-made products more expensive in overseas markets.

The U.S. had a $220.3 billion trade deficit with the European Union (EU) last year, bringing in $632.9 billion worth of goods from EU countries, according to the office of U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer.

Richard Stevens, the executive director of research and product development at CME Group, wrote on Sept. 25 that the U.S. dollar “has shown relative stability” so far this year, noting persistent inflation led the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates by a quarter point last month.

Markets expecting future rate hikes and higher borrowing costs going forward “neutralizes the net impact on the dollar,” Stevens noted.

The global bond market sell-off has not exempted European nations, as rising public debt on the continent and elevated energy costs during the conflicts in Iran and Ukraine have led to investors fleeing.

France’s and Germany’s respective 10-year bond yields closed at roughly $4.86 and $3.50 on Monday, dozens of basis points above where they stood before the U.S. and Israel launched their war on Iran in late February.

The euro also fell after Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called a snap election for Nov. 29 on Monday.

Sánchez, a left-wing critic of President Trump who has been in office since 2018, scheduled the election after protests swept across his country amid a housing crisis.
